title: Verifier-Guided Bounded Repair for LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Paired Confirmatory Study Under Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (CAND-2026-001) that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) on deterministic-invariant acceptance for intent→configuration NetOps tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we executed 200 preregistered tasks with a hosted model declared as gpt-5-mini (model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset). Provider-call accounting records 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair (201 model calls total). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired contingency counts: n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 (exact-binomial two-sided formulation); paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair that corrected a required-sequence ordering breach in an ‘‘extreme’’ difficulty task. We present the preregistration, complete execution accounting, paired analysis, a localized failure diagnosis anchored in archived validator traces, and bounded limitations supported by the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness for such workflows requires generated configurations to satisfy deterministic invariants (workflow ordering, allowed-touched-field constraints, group-level availability, and syntactic/semantic constraints). While prototype systems and benchmarks illustrate feasibility, the marginal effect of verifier-triggered bounded repair on an identical initial generation remains underexplored.

This study addresses that gap with a preregistered paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) that enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics: for every task the identical single sampled candidate was deterministically reused by both the baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator may trigger ≤1 repair) episodes. Under this design any paired difference arises solely from the deterministic verifier plus the single permitted repair; it does not reflect independent guarded first-pass generations, prompt-engineering differences, or multi-sample selection. The principal estimand is the per-task paired difference in binary acceptance by a deterministic verifier (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). We report complete execution accounting (200 shared initial generations, 1 repair), confirmatory paired inference, and a focused diagnostic for the lone repaired pair using archived validator traces.
sections.related_work:
Prior work demonstrates active research on intent→configuration pipelines and on integrating generators with verification or test-based repair loops. NetConfEval and related intent→config prototypes show that mapping natural-language or intent specifications to device configurations is an active benchmarking area and that LLM-based generation is a practical research avenue [1]. Deterministic configuration verifiers provide operational oracles for syntactic and semantic invariants and are commonly used in configuration-synthesis evaluation [2]. In adjacent domains, generate→validate→repair patterns and test-in-the-loop program-repair studies show that validating generated artifacts against executable checks and using repairs can improve artifact correctness in software-engineering contexts [4], but those demonstrations are not direct evidence for NetOps because network invariants, multi-device sequencing, and group-level availability introduce distinct dependency structures.

Tool-augmented agent designs and studies of LLM/tool coupling emphasize architecture and integration challenges when granting models access to external solvers or validators; such work motivates verifier-mediated NetOps workflows but also highlights the importance of oracle specification and artifacted evaluation [6]. Reporting and preregistration guidance for studies using LLMs informed our preregistration and archival choices [3].

Synthesis. The verified literature supports three modest points relevant to our study: (i) intent→configuration pipelines and benchmarks have been prototyped and evaluated in research settings [1]; (ii) deterministic verifiers constitute appropriate operational oracles for many correctness properties in configuration synthesis [2]; and (iii) generate→validate→repair architectures are a promising pattern in adjacent domains but require NetOps-specific empirical evaluation to quantify repair effects in multi-device sequencing contexts [4],[6]. Our paired, shared_initial_candidate experiment is designed to measure the narrower repair-only effect that arises when identical initial candidates are deterministically reused across conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration. The study design and analysis plan were preregistered (CAND-2026-001) before any model calls. The preregistration fixed a confirmatory paired binary estimand (per-task verifier acceptance, baseline vs guarded), N = 200 tasks, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task deterministically reused by both episodes), at most one automated repair call per task, primary failed-call treatment complete_pair_primary, the exact two-sided McNemar confirmatory test, and a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistration artifact is archived in the execution manifest.

Task generator and verifier oracle. Tasks were produced by a deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) with fixed selection indices as preregistered; each manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies. The deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is the operational oracle: it parses commands, enforces allowed_touched_fields, checks required_sequence ordering, evaluates group-level invariants (final_group_constraints, minimum_active_in_groups), and returns full_intent_constraint_validation only when all encoded constraints are satisfied. The verifier emits structured tracer outputs archived and used for scoring and the diagnostic reported below.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and sampling notes. The adapter contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each pair the exact same initial generation (one sampled candidate) was provided to both baseline and guarded episodes. The model-configuration record declares the requested model as gpt-5-mini and records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling therefore remains a possible background property even though the experiment used a single initial sample per pair by design.

Sanitizer and bounded repair policy. For each task a deterministic formatting sanitizer ran prior to verifier parsing. If the verifier reported invariant violations, the guarded logic could invoke at most one automated repair call to the hosted model with a repair prompt constructed from the archived validator trace (as preregistered). Repair calls were counted against the maximum_model_calls budget; deterministic reconciliation records exactly one repair call across all pairs. Persistent unparsables after sanitizer plus the single permitted repair were handled per preregistered missingness rules (primary analysis applied complete_pair_primary).

Provider-call accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts are authoritative: shared_initial_generation = 200, repair = 1, hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, cache_hit_count = 0. These stage-level counts match the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the recorded single repair invocation.

Statistical analysis. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar computed from discordant pair counts n10 and n01 using the exact-binomial-tail formulation implemented by the archived analysis executor. For the paired absolute risk difference we computed a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All analysis code and bootstrap parameters are archived; re-running the archived analysis executor reproduces the reported contingency counts, p-value, and CI.

These numeric results and all analysis artifacts are archived and reproduce when the archived analysis executor is rerun on the raw results.

Single repair event and localized diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked exactly one automated repair. Archived validator traces for the repaired pair indicate the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence ordering constraint: the task's difficulty metadata included required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3, difficulty.level = "extreme". The verifier trace records validation_before.violation_codes showing the ordering breach and validation_after.valid = true once the bounded repair was applied. The repair converted a sequenced-dependency failure into a configuration accepted by the deterministic verifier (score = 1, scorer_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION"). These per-episode tracer fields in the archived artifacts constitute the evidence that the single observed paired improvement resulted from a verifier-triggered repair that enacted the required reordering.

Missingness, contamination, and consistency. The run recorded no preregistered exclusions and no persistent unparsables; missingness summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zeros for other missingness categories. Deterministic reconciliation indicates pair_accounting_consistent = true and all_deterministic_consistency_checks_passed = true.
sections.discussion:
What was measured: a repair-only estimand. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the experiment isolates only the marginal effect of permitting a verifier-triggered bounded repair on an identical initial candidate. The observed difference (one corrected pair) therefore arises solely from the deterministic verifier and the single permitted repair; it is not evidence that constrained prompts, independent guarded first-pass generations, or multi-sample selection would produce the same or larger improvements.

Interpreting the sparse-discordant regime. The preregistration targeted detection of moderate absolute paired increases (~10–15 percentage points) at N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions (~45–65%). The realized baseline success rate (199/200 = 99.5%) placed the analysis in a sparse-discordant regime with only one discordant pair. In this regime the exact two-sided McNemar p-value gives limited directional evidence (p = 1.0 for n = 1, k = 1), while the paired-bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015] quantifies the upper bound of plausible absolute improvement attributable to repair under the repair-only estimand. Operationally, unexpectedly high baseline performance reduces sensitivity to detect small marginal effects; the archived bootstrap CI provides a principled bound on the maximum plausible repair-only absolute improvement consistent with our data.

Failure-mode interpretation and difficulty stratification. Representative task manifests include difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). The archived representative subset spans required_command_count values 3–9 and changed_interface_count up to 3. The single baseline failure and corresponding repaired pair associate with an extreme composite difficulty (required_command_count = 9, changed_interface_count = 3), consistent with the exploratory preregistered hypothesis that multi-device sequencing and dependency complexity concentrate residual failures. This localized observation supports a narrowly scoped inferential statement: verifier-guided bounded repair can address ordering/dependency violations that are expressible in the verifier's required_sequence invariants, particularly in complex multi-step workflows.

Operational implications and qualification. Artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained operational conclusion: in this synthetic deterministic task bank using the declared model gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a verifier-triggered bounded repair corrected a localized multi-step ordering fault in one extreme task. This is direct evidence that bounded repair can remedy certain ordering/dependency violations in generated configurations when those violations are captured by the verifier's manifest-encoded invariants. It is not evidence that bounded repair will correct runtime-only dataplane omissions, vendor-specific runtime semantics outside the verifier's model, or adversarially poisoned contexts. Those broader operational claims require additional experiments (multi-model comparisons, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, adversarial contamination testing, and live-device/dataplane emulation).

Threats to validity. Internal: the paired shared_initial_candidate design intentionally isolates repair effects but does not address prompt sensitivity, model-sampling variability, or the potential benefits of independent guarded generations. Construct: the verifier enforces encoded syntactic and ordering invariants but does not substitute for dataplane emulation or vendor-specific runtime semantics. External: single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic deterministic task bank limit cross-model and production generality. Statistical: with only one discordant pair the power to detect small repair-only effects is limited; the paired-bootstrap CI quantifies that uncertainty.

Recommended next evaluation steps (evidence-grounded). To expand operational relevance while preserving verifier-based correctness guarantees, subsequent studies should (a) evaluate multi-model and multi-sample guarded semantics (remove shared_initial_candidate constraint) to measure the combined effects of constrained prompting and selection; (b) include live dataplane emulation or vendor-specific execution to evaluate invariants not fully captured by static verifier models; and (c) perform controlled adversarial/poisoning experiments to characterize robustness to contaminated retrieval/context. These directions are consistent with unresolved questions and candidate gaps identified in the verified literature synthesis and are explicitly beyond the present repair-only estimand.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered bounded repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In 200 synthetic deterministic tasks using the declared model gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, baseline acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; a single automated repair corrected a multi-device required-sequence ordering violation. Paired absolute risk difference = 0.005 with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) and exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. Artifact-grounded evidence therefore supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded bounded repair can correct localized ordering faults in this synthetic verifier-backed setting. Broader operational claims require further experiments (multi-model studies, independent-first-pass guarded semantics, adversarial contamination testing, live-device/dataplane emulation).

Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Deterministic verifier (oracle): deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). Humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Archived provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are available in the execution bundle for audit.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
